meta.title: agy-review: an independent reviewer that has to show its work
meta.desc: Code review, security review, task delegation and translation by Google Antigravity, from Claude Code, Codex or your terminal. Read-only, no permission prompts, every finding checked against your real code.
hero.title: An independent reviewer that has to show its work
hero.sub: Code review, security review, task delegation and translation by Google Antigravity. From Claude Code, Codex or your terminal. Read-only, no permission prompts, and every finding is checked against your real code.
hero.note: Runs on Bun or Node 18.18+. Your code is sent to Google's model: review only what you may share.
hero.chip2: Exit codes for agents and CI
term.title: Quick start
trust.title: Why the report is trustworthy
trust.sub: A model that reviews code will sometimes invent a problem. This tool never takes its word for anything.
trust.1.t: Quote it or it did not happen
trust.1.d: Every finding must carry the exact code it is about. The script looks that quote up in the real file.
trust.2.d: Invented findings are dropped and listed separately. A wrong line number is corrected, not trusted.
trust.3.d: The verdict, the counts and the CI gate are computed from verified findings only, never copied from the model.
trust.4.d: If findings were rejected, coverage is low or a model failed, the verdict is inconclusive and the exit code is 4.
proof.title: What a verified finding looks like
proof.sub: Real output on a small file with planted bugs, reviewed by Claude Sonnet 4.6 through Antigravity.
proof.ok: Verified: this exact code exists at line 6
proof.bad: Rejected: the quoted code was not found in the file
how.title: How a review runs
how.sub: Five steps, one script. Static targets never give the model any tool.
how.1.d: Review a diff, a branch, a file, a line range, one function or a snippet.
how.2.d: The script reads and numbers the code itself, or opens the repository behind a read-only guard.
how.3.d: The model you chose returns a strict JSON report: severity, priority, category, evidence, fix.
how.4.d: Quotes are found in your files, lines are corrected, inventions are rejected, secrets are redacted.
how.5.d: Markdown or JSON, stable finding ids, and an exit code that agents and CI can act on.
feat.title: Built for people and for agents
feat.1.d: Uncommitted changes, a branch, a commit, a file, a line range, one function by name, or code piped in from memory.
feat.2.d: OWASP and CWE mapping, exploitability, attack scenario, data flow, a secret and bad-pattern scanner, and the callers and callees of your code.
feat.3.d: Stable JSON, finding ids that survive line shifts, comparison with the previous report, and a gate: exit 10 when a verified high finding exists.
feat.4.d: List the models in your agy, pick one per project or globally, cross-check with several, and let effort be chosen automatically with the reason shown.
feat.5.d: Hand any self-contained task to Antigravity. Translate with tone, audience and glossary, and verify that code, URLs and placeholders survived.
feat.6.d: Skills for Claude Code and Codex, plus reviewer, security and worker sub-agents that any larger process can call.
graphify.title: Stop paying Claude and Codex tokens to refresh your graphify graph
graphify.sub: graphify updates now run on Antigravity, in the background, on every commit, merge, checkout and rebase. Your agent spends 0 tokens on them and you need no API key.
graphify.1.d: graphify's backend is pinned to a local server backed by Antigravity, so it can never fall back to your Opus, Fable or Codex session.
graphify.2.d: The hook starts the update in the background. In a real run git commit returned in 0.3 seconds and the graph updated in 22 seconds with one Antigravity call.
graphify.3.d: The model only reads text and answers text. graphify writes its own files, a prompt injection in a document cannot make the model do anything, and secrets are redacted.
graphify.note: It uses your Antigravity quota, so it is cheaper, not free. Images are not extracted on this path.
install.title: Install
install.sub: Pick your host. Nothing else is required besides Antigravity, git and Bun or Node.
install.verify: Verify on your machine: reads work, writes are blocked.
install.codex: Codex needs network access and write access to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli in its sandbox. The skill tells you exactly what is missing and never widens permissions itself.
install.agy: The guard is a normal Antigravity plugin. It does nothing unless a prompt contains AGY_READONLY_REVIEW, so your own agy sessions are unchanged.
use.title: Use it
use.sub: The same script behind every skill, command and sub-agent.
use.1: Review a function with its context
use.3: Translate with tone and a glossary
sec.title: Honest about its limits
sec.sub: Read this before you trust it with anything important.
sec.does.1: Static reviews, tasks and translations run agy with no tools in an empty folder: it cannot read or write your files.
sec.does.2: Agentic reviews run behind a deny-by-default guard hook, refuse to start without it, and warn if your working tree changed.
sec.does.3: Hard-coded secrets are redacted before anything is sent to a model.
sec.does.4: A CVE from a model is always labelled unverified. The tool never invents or confirms one.
sec.not.1: Not an OS sandbox. The guard filters commands; a determined prompt injection in reviewed code could look for a gap.
sec.not.2: Your code is sent to Google's model. Do not review what you may not share.
sec.not.3: Findings can be wrong. No findings never means secure.
sec.not.4: The agentic path with the real permission flag was not run by the author. Run verify once on your machine.
faq.title: Questions
faq.1.a: No. Static modes cannot. Agentic mode blocks writes and warns if your tree differs afterwards. It never commits, stashes or checks anything out, and it never fixes findings itself.
faq.2.a: The plugin is free and open source. Each review uses your own Antigravity quota.
faq.3.q: Is Bun faster than Node here?
faq.3.a: Not measurably. Startup was about 56 ms with Node and 64 ms with Bun on the author's Windows machine, and a review takes tens of seconds because of the model. Bun is the default, Node works the same.
faq.4.a: Run the models command and choose; the tool does not rank them for you. For critical code cross-check with two models: findings both report are marked.
faq.5.q: What if Gemini refuses a security prompt?
faq.5.a: Its content filter sometimes does. If you did not pick a model, the tool retries once with a non-Gemini model and says so.
faq.6.q: Can an agent run it in a loop?
faq.6.a: Yes. Review, fix the P0 and P1 findings, review again with the previous report, and stop on exit code 0. Exit code 4 is not a pass.
faq.7.q: How do I update to a new version?
faq.7.a: Run the update check, then update the plugin for your host and refresh the guard and the graphify hooks. The README has the exact commands for Claude Code, Codex and a plain clone.
